capabilities: Convert a whole image or a drawn rectangular region to LaTeX
Load images by drag-and-drop, file browse, or clipboard paste
Copy the resulting LaTeX to the clipboard
Cache the ~100 MB model locally so repeat conversions work offline
Swap in any compatible Hugging Face VisionEncoderDecoder model via settings
disambiguation: Not a math renderer or calculator; it only extracts LaTeX from image regions using OCR.
extras: The model (~100 MB) is downloaded from Hugging Face on first use, so one-time internet access is needed; the manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The README limits accuracy to clean, isolated formulas rather than dense multi-formula pages.
motivation: The author built it because retyping equations is tedious and error-prone, and online converters are slow, require accounts, and send images to someone else's server.
problem: Retyping equations is tedious and error-prone, and online image-to-LaTeX converters need accounts, send data to third-party servers, and require leaving Obsidian.

relations.evidence: Math-Convert embeds FormulaNet, a 20 M-parameter vision-to-sequence model, and runs it locally

summary: Converts selected regions of images into LaTeX formulas using a small OCR model that runs offline in WebAssembly.
